metrics.prompt: Review our implementation of context ofr inferrence in sketch/sketch7 and report how it functions. List any issues you see. Make recommendations on architectural improvements.

findings: Payload Assembly: Builder.Build constructs a Payload containing static/dynamic Sections and a trimmed Message transcript derived from session history (context.go:52).

Block-Based Message Trimming: trimMessages groups history into blocks to preserve tool call/result pairs. It retains the most recent messages up to a count limit (default 12) and forces inclusion of the latest user message as an anchor to maintain conversational context (context.go:99-130).

Repo Context Caching & Refresh: RepoContextCache.Summary scans the filesystem and git status, caching results and refreshing based on interaction turn count to minimize I/O overhead per inference (repo.go:29-54).

Dynamic Section Generation: BuildSections iterates over agent context projections to generate system prompts covering cognitive state, workflow progress, binding status, and repo context (sections.go:15-49).

Linear History Scans: Functions like InteractionTurnCount (repo.go:107), latestContextSnapshot (repo.go:56), and workflowProgress (sections.go:93) perform O(N) linear scans over history.Records, which degrades performance as sessions grow.
Global Mutable State: sections.go:13 declares a package-level var defaultRepoCache, which breaks thread-safety for concurrent sessions and complicates isolated testing.
Count-Based vs Token Budget: Trimming relies on a raw message count limit rather than token counts, leading to unpredictable context window utilization given variable-length tool outputs.
Hardcoded Workflow Logic: Workflow states and transition rules are hardcoded in sections.go:106, tightly coupling context generation to specific workflow definitions.
Deprecated Hash Algorithm: context.go:238 uses SHA1 for HashContent, which is cryptographically weak and generally discouraged even for non-security checksums.
unknowns: How the Payload struct is consumed downstream and mapped to specific LLM provider APIs.
The exact schema and size constraints of logs.SessionHistory and runtime.SessionView from the adjacent runtime package.
Whether the application runs multiple sessions concurrently in the same process, which would exacerbate the global cache thread-safety issue.
How token limits or context window sizes are currently enforced or communicated to the Builder.
